## Historical audit: S0275

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/preparation/second_smoke/historical_r1_C2_start/development/commons_109923183/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below are JSONL lines in this file. The supplied observations contain no image pixels for independent inspection.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Goal: H `model_request`, line 1 | Reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching camera, framing, placement and materials. The student’s inventory interprets the scene as a chaise, pillow, label, paneled room, window and curtain, and cropped cane chair; these are student interpretations, not independently verified image contents (H `model_response`, line 3). |
| First build: H `model_response` and `execute`, lines 3–4 | Created multiple named assets and child parts: seat, head, arms, rails, legs and pillow, plus architecture and chair fragment. Color assignments, stripe rods and floor seams approximate materials and texture. Parenting establishes hierarchy, not verified physical connections. Camera and two area lights were configured. |
| First validation and revision: `execution_result`, line 9; H `model_request`, line 11; H `model_response` and `execute`, lines 13–14 | Build and render returned success and the render was supplied for comparison. The student reported a small chaise, light floor, thin seat, insufficient arm fill and repetitive molding. It widened the upholstery, darkened colors, changed panel dimensions and camera/lights. These discrepancies are the student’s assessment, not an independent visual finding. |
| Second validation and revision: `execution_result`, line 19; H `model_response` and `execute`, lines 23–24 | Second render succeeded. The student reported a need for a more rectangular cushion, square pillow, fuller arm, darker surfaces and a more overhead view. The third program used rounded boxes for cushion and pillow, expanded side panels, changed camera elevation and reduced lighting. Object pose and part contact were not independently geometrically checked. |
| Outcome: `execution_result`, line 29; `select`, line 30 | Third build and render returned `ok: true`, and step 3 was selected. This is **technical execution success**, not demonstrated reconstruction accuracy. No post-third-render student comparison or formal visual score is visible. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher message, teacher diagnosis or proposed teacher update appears in the supplied student trajectory; receipt or adoption cannot be claimed. The student made two render-informed revisions autonomously. The recorded Codex sessions show no tool calls, while the external runner executed the programs (H `codex_session`, lines 2, 12 and 22; `execute`, lines 4, 14 and 24).

**Transferable lesson:** A successful render permits comparison and targeted iteration, but does not establish visual fidelity or correct part connections. **Task-specific hypothesis:** the student’s proposed overhead camera and fuller upholstery might improve this particular match; the final image was not independently inspected here, so improvement, material realism, occlusion, contact, framing and lighting remain unresolved. There is no evidence of an empty patch, algorithmic failure or technical interruption in the recorded executions.
